'''Alex Alcalde''' was a Decipher-era [[Squadron Members|Squadron Member]], listed as Gold 31 from Terre Haute, IN.<ref name="sm-fan" /> The published fan table marks the slot Retired after Decipher's SWCCG run.

A History graduate student at Indiana State University, formerly of Toronto, he started playing in January 1996. In May 1997 he led two carloads of Toronto players to the Rochester Open. In Terre Haute he built a group of about 40 players and a regional website, the [[Corellian Engineering Corporation (fan site)|Corellian Engineering Corporation]]. His motto: "When both Luck and Skill fail you, kick over the table."<ref name="decsq-prof" />

Decipher recruited volunteer Squadron Members in the 1990s to promote SWCCG locally (tournaments, demos, player support). "FL" is printed on some slots in the surviving tables; the tables do not spell out the abbreviation.

== Other sourced notes ==

Gold 31 FL, Indianapolis, Indiana. [[Radio Free Decipher]] broadcast 9 (26 February 1999) included a squadron and ambassador call-in with Chris Swearingen, Alex Alcalde, [[Carl Mike Hardy|Mike Hardy]], and [[Guy Kargl]].<ref name="rfd-09">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QU24jFxZsHM Radio Free Decipher 09], Player's Council (26 February 1999). Guests Chris Swearingen, [[Alex Alcalde]], Mike Hardy, and [[Guy Kargl]]. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-QU24jFxZsHM Internet Archive].</ref>

He posted two [[Young Jedi]] lists on the [[Corellian Engineering Corporation (fan site)]] as '''Gold 31''': ''Wizards!'' (Jedi) and ''All Droids All the time!'' (Sith). Archived copies: [https://www.geocities.ws/plarathas/decks/jedi1.html jedi1.html] · [https://web.archive.org/web/20011202101302/http://www.geocities.com/CollegePark/Plaza/9433/decks/jedi1.html Wayback, 2 December 2001]; [https://www.geocities.ws/plarathas/decks/sith1.html sith1.html] · [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009020148/https://www.geocities.ws/plarathas/decks/sith1.html Wayback, 9 October 2026].
